text:
maya: Quick thread  we need a concise playbook for the long-term routing + multi-region + tenant-isolation roadmap to present at the Q3 roadmap review. Can we lock priorities + measurable gates today?

owen: I split into three product initiatives to keep messaging simple:
- Reside = data residency / compliance (EU/UK/CA)
- EdgeFast = low-latency edge (APAC + maybe Tokyo/Singapore POPs)
- Shield = dedicated tenant isolation (reserved pools / soft-eviction)

sasha: For each we should publish: acceptance criteria, rollout model, cost delta, and customer onboarding flow. Quick draft of acceptance criteria below.

maya: please. short bullets are fine.

sasha: Acceptance drafts:
- Reside:
  - All customer data "at rest" and logs for the routed requests remain in-region (including backups)
  - KMS keys provisioned in-region; no cross-region key use for resident customers
  - Compliance checklist signed by SOC/Legal for the customer (manual gate)
  - Test: synthetic writes/reads show 0 cross-region egress over a 24h window

- EdgeFast:
  - Latency: p50 < 80ms and p95 < 180ms for traffic originating in target APAC metro
  - Capacity: system can soak 2x observed peak QPS for 10 minutes without request queueing >100ms
  - Fallback: when capacity exceeded, route to nearest region with documented QoS degradation message
  - Test: load test with representative prompts and Llama/Redwood-verified model variants

- Shield:
  - Isolation: single-tenant average CPU steal <2% over 1h windows and memory working set limits enforced
  - Cost/Quality: model token-cost delta to multi-tenant baseline <12% for same config
  - SLA: isolation-tier SLA 99.9% availability on reserved capacity (billing tier dependent)
  - Test: tenant-specific noisy-neighbor synthetic workloads do not increase latency above threshold for neighbor tenants

li: ops question  how do we validate "no cross-region egress" automatically? we can add an infra check that scans flow logs and flags external egress IPs per-customer.

ops-bot: network-checker: existing tool can run daily scans and emit alerts; recommend adding a 24h verification job before GA cutover for each customer.

owen: Rollout model proposal (keep names distinct from usual pilot/beta/ga):
- Alpha-pilot: internal + 1 trusted customer. manual onboarding, weekend cutover window, full ops presence
- Controlled-roll: up to 10 customers across segments; runtime flags + traffic shaping (header-based sampling) + automated health gating
- Public launch: self-serve in Console, public pricing, SLA and runbook published

maya: Controlled-roll detail: we should use header-based routing so we can shift traffic slices without DNS TTL issues. Example rule (concept):
```
if request.headers['X-Routing-Mode'] == 'edgefast-ctrl' then route->apac-pop-1
else route->regional-default
```

sasha: Good. also include synthetic evaluation gates for model quality:
- For any model variant used at edge/shield, run the evaluation suite on a shared prompt set. Release gate: no >5% drop in primary metric (e.g., helpfulness/f1/rouge) vs baseline.

owen: Pricing & packaging thoughts:
- Reside: no additional infra charge but premium contract + compliance onboarding fee (cover legal ops)
- EdgeFast: usage-based + small fixed monthly POP reservation fee (helps pre-warm capacity)
- Shield: paid add-on with minimum commit (e.g., 3-month reserved vGPU pool) + higher token price for isolated capacity

li: ops dependencies to resolve before Controlled-roll:
- KMS in-region automation + proof for legal
- Console UI toggle for route affinity and reservation purchases
- Metrics + dashboard templates for rollout (latency, error-rate, egress, token-cost)

maya: risks to call out in the deck:
- Cost vs latency tradeoff: pre-warm GPUs and edge POPs are expensive; sales will want clear numbers
- Model parity: not all model variants may be available on quantized/edge infra; quality regressions possible
- Migration friction: customer endpoints, VPNs, or SSO might need reconfig during cutover

sasha: propose a short checklist we can include on the roadmap slide. (one-liner items)
- Contracting ready (legal + SOC signoff)
- Ops runbook exists and tested (rollback <30m)
- Synthetic evals pass
- Billing/console flows validated
- Customer onboarding guide written

maya: action items & owners:
- maya: draft 2-slide roadmap + one-pager acceptance criteria (due Wed)
- owen: cost model for each initiative + sample pricing for Shield (due Tue)
- sasha: synthetic eval suite spec & baseline metrics (due Tue)
- li: infra dependency list + target delivery dates (due Thu)
- ops-bot: schedule daily network-checker job and produce template alert thresholds (ops-bot:done -> ping)

ops-bot: scheduled job created: network-checker/daily-residency-verify. alert thresholds: egress>0 flagged, latency-p95>threshold triggers paging for controlled-roll.

owen: one last question  for Shield, do we support soft-eviction migrating heavy tenants mid-flight? that impacts rollback strategy.

li: suggested approach: prefer proactive isolation (reserve capacity); if eviction needed, move tenant to degraded-mode with clear API response + warm standby region; automated migration should be last resort.

maya: awesome. I'll synthesize and post the slides here. If anyone has objections to the acceptance numbers above speak up now or send edits to the doc. :raised_hands:
